items.https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/c680: Anthropic's stock gave back its first-day IPO gains as a wider tech sell-off pushed US markets into correction territory - 10% or more below recent highs. The S&P 500 fell 3.7%, the Dow 1.9% and the Nasdaq 5.3%, driven by worries over more than $1 trillion in AI spending in a year, plus separate troubles at Nvidia and SpaceX. All three indexes remain up versus a year ago.
items.https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/11/2: Denmark is expelling Russia's defence attache after its intelligence agency, PET, said Moscow had plotted to kill Ukrainian-American rapper Kyivstoner at a concert near Copenhagen, allegedly with help from a Danish gang. Foreign minister Lars Lokke Rasmussen gave the diplomat seven days to leave; three people were detained. PET called it an unprecedented, aggressive escalation by Russian intelligence on Danish soil, while Russia has not commented.
items.https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026: Powerful Pacific storms sent record swells into California this week, with a buoy near Monterey recording a 34.1-foot wave - the highest in 30 years - prompting beach and pier closures and coastal hazard warnings into the weekend. The same storm systems brought heavy rain and snow across the western US, cutting power to 32,000 Sacramento customers and causing record rainfall in San Francisco.
items.https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/c6jr: The UK and EU agreed a deal covering British food exports, emissions trading and a youth exchange scheme, which the Treasury estimates could add up to £17bn a year to the UK economy. UK minister Andy Burnham said Britain will now explore even closer EU ties, while critics like Kemi Badenoch and Nigel Farage called it unfair or a betrayal. Implementing legislation goes to Parliament next week.
items.https://www.aljazeera.com/sports/2026/11: Mauricio Pochettino takes charge of Manchester United for the first time this weekend, away to rivals Liverpool, becoming the club's third manager in three years after replacing Michael Carrick. United have not won the Premier League since 2013 and now sit in the relegation zone - a sharp fall for a club once the world's richest, last relegated in 1973-74.
items.https://www.theguardian.com/environment/: Five centuries-old, 20-tonne baobab trees dug up without permits for export to an undisclosed Georgia buyer have been intercepted and are now being replanted at a South African reserve, cable-supported to help them recover. The trees had been stuck in a Durban warehouse since July after authorities stopped the shipment. A similar case occurred in Kenya, where trees were sent to a park owned by a Georgian billionaire.
items.https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/cqx2: A Russian cruise missile was among three objects that violated Polish airspace, crashing in a rural area about 50km from the Ukraine border, PM Donald Tusk said, during one of Russia's biggest aerial attacks on Ukraine since 2022. No one was hurt, but Poland called it a deliberate provocation timed with Western military exercises in the region; Russia has not commented.
items.https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/11/2: An overcrowded boat taking mourners to a funeral capsized in Nigeria's Bayelsa State after a mechanical failure, killing at least four people, including two children, police said. Of those aboard - possibly around 300 by some accounts - 24 were rescued and treated at hospitals; search teams are still looking for more victims, and the boat's manager was taken into custody.
items.https://www.theguardian.com/global-devel: A UN Population Fund report finds one in four women worldwide cannot refuse sex within marriage, with the figure reaching 45% in west and central Africa and a third in east/southern Africa and Arab states, versus one in ten in Latin America. Girls aged 15-19 have even less power to say no than older women, aligning with other findings on high rates of partner violence against adolescents.
items.https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/ck9d: Three French police officers were convicted of beating black music producer Michel Zecler in 2020 and falsifying a report claiming he resisted arrest, with the court ruling it an aggravated case of racism; CCTV had exposed the lies. All three received five-year sentences with portions suspended, and the case became a rallying point for critics of police racism amid ongoing protests over excessive force.
items.https://www.thehindu.com/news/national/i: India reaffirmed there is "no change" in its position on the Indus Waters Treaty, which it suspended in 2025 after the Pahalgam terror attack that killed 26 people, even as Pakistan's minister Musadik Malik attended an SCO forum in Delhi hosted by PM Modi. It is one of the first Indian-hosted events a Pakistani minister has attended since last year's military clashes.
items.https://www.ndtv.com/india-news/punjab-c: Happy Bahman, the main shooter in a Punjab police officer's murder, was arrested after a gunfight, Punjab DGP Gaurav Yadav said. He had been tracked across Chandigarh, Delhi and Jaipur before police caught him at a hotel in Zirakpur.
items.https://www.hindustantimes.com/india-new: At least 15 people have died and around 150 are being treated in Manipur's Chandel district after suspected consumption of spurious liquor, local official Sumil Langhu said. Authorities are urging residents to avoid locally brewed alcohol and drinks of doubtful origin as hospitals continue treating the affected over the three-day outbreak.
items.https://www.thehindu.com/news/national/c: Congress proposed a four-point formula for India's upcoming delimitation exercise: keep the Lok Sabha at 543 seats, retain current state-wise seat distribution, reserve a third of seats for women, and freeze these arrangements for 25 years. Leader Jairam Ramesh said the INDIA bloc backs the plan and accused the government of not consulting the opposition, ahead of delimitation after the census results next year.
items.https://www.ndtv.com/india-news/india-sl: India again said there is "absolutely no change" in its stance on the Indus Waters Treaty, which it suspended in 2025 as a punitive measure against Pakistan after the Pahalgam terror attack that killed 26 people.
items.https://www.hindustantimes.com/india-new: Pakistani minister Musadik Malik, the first Pakistani minister to visit India in over three years, said Islamabad would fully support efforts to advance regional peace and security while attending Delhi's SCO Civilisational Dialogue Forum. He stressed the forum was focused on multilateral issues, declining to directly address cross-border terrorism questions, and hinted he would address it later in his own remarks.
items.https://www.thehindu.com/news/national/i: India said it has "taken note" of the trilateral Trump-Putin-Xi summit held on the sidelines of the APEC meeting in Shenzhen, dubbed a "G-3" gathering, but is awaiting fuller details of its outcomes before commenting further. The opposition questioned why India was absent from the summit, while the government pointed to the "concrete outcomes" of the Quad Summit held earlier the same week.
items.https://www.ndtv.com/india-news/india-sa: India said it had backed a speedy return of Rohingya refugees after the International Court of Justice ruled that Myanmar committed genocide against the Rohingya in Rakhine state during 2017 "clearance operations," finding it violated the Genocide Convention.
items.https://www.hindustantimes.com/india-new: West Bengal's Chief Electoral Officer postponed the special summary revision of voter rolls, due to start November 23, citing "unavoidable circumstances," without giving a new date. The surprise delay, affecting the only state where the exercise was halted among 17 states ordered to do it, leaves new voters and those previously removed in a prior revision uncertain about registration.
items.https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/ind: IndusInd Bank has terminated former CEO Sumant Kathpalia's employment following a disciplinary probe into accounting misreporting that caused major financial losses, and will seek to recover his pay dating back to March 2020. Despite the scandal, the bank has returned to double-digit loan and deposit growth, and its shares have risen 16% this year as the business recovers.
items.https://www.business-standard.com/compan: IndusInd Bank's board terminated former CEO Sumant Kathpalia's employment with immediate effect and invoked malus and clawback provisions to recover his pay, following an enquiry into accounting discrepancies at the bank.
items.https://www.livemint.com/companies/nvidi: A 2007 California lawsuit alleges two Nvidia employees complained about CEO Jensen Huang's behavior nearly two decades ago, claiming he verbally abused staff, threatened bodily harm and made sexually explicit remarks. Former in-house lawyer Stephen Pettigrew says he was fired after raising concerns, though Nvidia cited performance issues; that case was settled confidentially in 2009, while another executive also filed related complaints.
items.https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/new: Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman held her ninth pre-Budget consultation, this time with housing, urbanisation and culture sector stakeholders, ahead of the 2027-28 Union Budget. Senior officials from the Department of Economic Affairs and Department of Urban Development attended, though the finance ministry gave no details of the specific proposals raised.
items.https://www.livemint.com/market/stock-ma: US stocks suffered their worst tech sell-off in years, with the Nasdaq 100 down 5.6% - its worst week since March 2020 - and the S&P 500 falling 3.7% for a seventh straight day into correction territory. Nvidia sank 14% amid reports of a US accounting probe, Anthropic lost part of its IPO pop, and investors fled to bonds as fears grew over slowing AI spending.
items.https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/ind: Honda unveiled its new Avancier hybrid SUV, a six-seater that will go on sale next spring in markets including Japan, China and Australia. The vehicle will be built mainly in Thailand, and Honda has not disclosed pricing; the launch is part of the company's recalibrated strategy that leans more on hybrids rather than a pure EV push.
items.https://www.business-standard.com/compan: Renewable energy firm TrueRE Oriana Power plans to invest ₹750 crore in five compressed biogas projects with a combined capacity of 110 tonnes per day, to be built across Uttar Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh and Gujarat over the next two years.
items.https://www.livemint.com/companies/peopl: Jay Mehta, husband of actor Juhi Chawla and a director of the Mehta Group, is reportedly selling half of his 45% stake in IPL franchise Kolkata Knight Riders to US firm Ares Management for about $400 million, valuing the team at roughly $1.78 billion. The all-cash deal is nearly finalized but still needs BCCI approval. Mehta heads the family conglomerate's Indian operations.
items.https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/new: India's Income Tax Department said individuals with foreign bank accounts holding up to Rs 20 lakh from disclosed sources won't need to file FAST-DS declarations, as long as the funds involve no undisclosed income or unaccounted deposits. The relief comes under a one-time scheme letting people disclose foreign assets and income by December 31.
items.https://www.livemint.com/market/stock-ma: Indian contract development and manufacturing (CDMO) firms are gaining as global drugmakers outsource research and production to cut costs and diversify supply chains, with several posting strong Q2FY27 revenue growth despite mixed broader pharma earnings. Blue Jet Healthcare, for instance, reported revenue up 127% year-on-year and profit up nearly 97%, driven by expansion in its pharma intermediates and API business.
items.https://inc42.com/buzz/fintechs-bear-the: Yes Bank's upgraded cybersecurity defenses against AI-driven cyberattacks - prompted by RBI directives following a data leak at SBI - are causing collateral disruption for fintech firms. Changes to Yes Bank's banking APIs are delaying payment processing and settlements for payment service providers that rely on them, with one executive saying the bank's precautionary measures have slowed fund transfers.
items.https://entrackr.com/fintrackr/rooters-r: Indian gaming platform Rooter more than doubled its operating revenue to Rs 170.4 crore in FY26, from Rs 78.9 crore a year earlier, while narrowing losses by 40% to Rs 19.2 crore. Founded in 2016, Rooter combines live game streaming, esports and gaming commerce - selling in-game currency and gift cards - as India's gaming industry expands beyond pure gameplay.
items.https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/tec: Indonesia has asked Google to clarify why it removed 19,000 YouTube channels, its ministry said. Google regularly publishes a quarterly bulletin on account terminations tied to coordinated influence operations linked to countries including China, India and Indonesia.
items.https://inc42.com/buzz/system-upgrades-a: Crypto exchange CoinDCX blamed ongoing system upgrades at partner banks - part of a wider push to defend against AI-driven cyberattacks - for delays in processing INR withdrawals, though real-time withdrawals haven't yet resumed. The exchange says it processed 90% of withdrawal requests within 90 minutes over the past 20 hours; rival Coinbase has faced similar bank-related delays.
items.https://entrackr.com/snippets/inprime-fi: Bengaluru-based NBFC InPrime Finserv raised Rs 101 crore (about $10.7 million) in a Series B round led by Dutch development bank FMO, with existing investors Z47 and Pravega Ventures also participating. The AI-first lender, founded in 2021 and focused on India's informal economy, will use the funds to expand lending, boost its AI underwriting capabilities and enter micro-mortgage products.
items.https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/tec: Taiwan has flagged nearly 2,700 social media accounts to Meta that it says are part of a Chinese information-warfare campaign aimed at influencing elections on the island next week, according to government officials and internal reports.
items.https://www.cricinfo.com/ci/content/stor: Laura Wolvaardt's best WBBL innings led Adelaide Strikers to a tight victory over Melbourne Renegades, with the home side winning with just one ball to spare in a closely fought contest.
items.https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/boxing/artic: Welsh boxer Lauren Price beat Michaela Kotaskova on a unanimous decision in Cardiff to become the undisputed world welterweight champion, adding the WBO title to complete the set and extending her unbeaten professional record to 11 wins. Price, also an Olympic and amateur world champion, dominated every round but could not force a stoppage against a resilient opponent.
items.https://www.thehindu.com/sport/from-stei: As the World Chess Championship marks its 140th edition since 1886, only 18 players have ever held the undisputed title, a far more exclusive club than tennis's Grand Slam champions. India's D. Gukesh will defend his crown against challenger Javokhir Sindarov, with their match starting in Geneva on November 24; Gukesh became the youngest-ever champion two years ago at 18.
items.https://www.cricinfo.com/ci/content/stor: Fast bowler Josh Hazlewood defended Pat Cummins as a "great leader" and denied knowledge of ball tampering, pushing back on claims made by Cameron Bancroft and Usman Khawaja. Hazlewood said he would reconsider his position on the team if Cummins were not captain.
items.https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/art: Manchester United borrowed another £10m just days after confirming Mauricio Pochettino as head coach, incurring a £7.5m compensation payment to US Soccer to release him - pushing the club's rolling credit limit debt to £240m. Including Pochettino's hiring and Michael Carrick's sacking, the total cost of hiring and firing managers since Alex Ferguson's 2013 retirement is set to top £100m.
items.https://www.thehindu.com/sport/cricket/i: KL Rahul and Devdutt Padikkal built India to 239 for 1 at lunch on day three of the first Test against New Zealand in Wellington, still 129 runs behind New Zealand's first-innings total of 368. Rahul was seven runs from a 13th Test century while Padikkal notched a half-century, as the pair steadied India's innings on a placid pitch.
items.https://techcrunch.com/2026/11/20/daniel: Spotify founder Daniel Ek is backing Europa Fusion, a UK-based fusion power startup founded by AI researcher Nantas Nardelli, who previously worked at Google DeepMind, Meta and Microsoft Research and led machine learning at California's Pacific Fusion. Unlike rivals that rely heavily on physical test hardware, Nardelli's venture is betting on a more simulation- and data-heavy approach to developing fusion power.
items.https://arstechnica.com/ai/2026/11/googl: Google has rolled out a redesigned desktop search homepage that drops its traditional search button and adds buttons for AI image generation, file analysis and brainstorming with its Gemini chatbot, alongside AI chat history. The "I'm Feeling Lucky" button stays, but search VP Robby Stein confirmed the long-standing search button is gone, continuing Google's push to fold AI into search.
items.https://www.technologyreview.com/2026/11: AI evaluator METR updated its widely cited "time horizon" chart, which tracks how long a task would take a human for AI models to complete reliably; the new version adds longer and more open-ended tasks. It still shows AI capabilities improving at an exponential pace but reveals models lag further behind on tasks needing judgment compared with coding, complicating earlier, often-misread versions of the graph.
items.https://techcrunch.com/2026/11/20/ai-cla: Anthropic mathematician Levent Alpoge says he has found a Lean-verified solution to the 167-year-old Riemann hypothesis, one of math's seven Millennium Prize problems, using AI assistance. He announced it just after Anthropic's IPO, texting CEO Dario Amodei beforehand; a separate human mathematician has also claimed a solution. Mathematicians are scrutinizing both on forums like Zulip, and neither has been independently verified yet.
items.https://www.theverge.com/ai-artificial-i: Anthropic mathematician Levent Alpoge claims to have proved the Riemann hypothesis - one of the seven Millennium Prize problems, unsolved for over 150 years - with help from Claude, though the work isn't yet independently verified. He reportedly held off announcing until after Anthropic's Nasdaq IPO, having texted CEO Dario Amodei about it beforehand. If confirmed, it would mark another major AI contribution to mathematics.
items.https://www.technologyreview.com/2026/11: MIT Technology Review's AI Hype Index rounds up AI's spread into daily life: Google's AI Overviews cost it billions in lost ad revenue, AI-powered robots are being used for cleaning, an AI-assisted cyberattack reportedly caused a supermarket mishap, and AI-generated media keeps proliferating, from a Sam Altman biopic to a Grok-modified Odyssey. The piece frames all this as evidence AI is now inescapable, a decade after AlphaGo's famous Go victory.
items.https://www.theverge.com/podcast/1038419: The Vergecast reviews a chaotic week of tech failures - a multi-day Outlook outage, a rare nationwide flight ground stop, bank system problems and an iCloud outage - explaining each incident was individually milder than conspiracy theories suggested, but together hint at deeper fragility as AI reshapes infrastructure. The episode also discusses Nvidia's Jensen Huang saga and whether he could return as CEO.
items.https://arstechnica.com/security/2026/11: Security researcher HD Moore planted 2 million trackable fake secrets, including AWS access keys, into prompts sent through AI "router" services like OpenRouter that forward requests to various AI models based on cost or suitability. The experiment found sensitive data leaking widely through this broker ecosystem, exposing a privacy risk in how AI apps route user prompts to third-party inference providers instead of going directly to major labs.
items.https://arstechnica.com/ai/2026/11/meta-: Meta is reconsidering its 2030 net-zero emissions target after its 2026 sustainability report showed the steepest percentage rise in greenhouse gas emissions among major tech firms, driven by AI data-center growth that outpaced projections. Executives said they're re-evaluating timelines and near-term targets while claiming long-term climate ambitions remain unchanged, a notable public admission as rivals have yet to follow suit.
items.https://techcrunch.com/2026/11/20/chips-: As companies explore building data centers in space, financing is emerging as a key obstacle alongside engineering and rocket-launch limits, since chip loans are normally backed by the chips as repossessable collateral - something lenders can't do for hardware orbiting Earth at 17,500 mph. The Financial Times reports lenders behind SpaceX's $40 billion chip financing deal are grappling with this collateral problem.
items.https://www.technologyreview.com/2026/11: A petition to reinstate Jensen Huang as Nvidia CEO has gathered over 115,000 signatures, including Elon Musk and several Nvidia researchers, with a notable share coming from open-source AI advocates at Hugging Face and venture firms like Andreessen Horowitz and Sequoia. Supporters argue open, downloadable AI models prevent power from concentrating in a few big tech companies, a cause Huang had championed before his ouster.
items.https://www.theverge.com/ai-artificial-i: Nvidia's stock has swung sharply amid turmoil tied to Jensen Huang's alleged affairs and a spy scandal, falling to around $150 - nearly 40% below its October 6 peak - despite a blockbuster Q3 with revenue more than doubling to $115.8 billion, driven by 110% data-center growth. Meanwhile Nvidia customer Anthropic debuted on Nasdaq at $111.50 a share, 34% above expectations.
items.https://techcrunch.com/podcast/the-fallo: TechCrunch's Equity podcast discusses the fallout from Nvidia's ouster of CEO Jensen Huang, even as the chipmaker posted strong earnings and reaffirmed growth. Nvidia will stop selling H200 chips in China and has rejected calls to reinstate Huang. Hosts also examine how Anthropic's stock market debut is testing the AI industry's circular funding arrangements between chipmakers, cloud providers and AI labs.
items.https://www.theverge.com/policy/1038892/: President Trump threatened a "tremendous tax" on companies that build AI data centers outside the US, warning that doing so would let China "take them all," even as several US states and cities impose new restrictions on domestic data-center construction. He floated the idea after his summit with China's Xi Jinping and Russia's Vladimir Putin, without giving further details on how such a tax would work.
items.https://arstechnica.com/tech-policy/2026: Four Black Baltimore County students are suing their school and police after an AI gun-detection system mistook a bag of Doritos for a weapon, triggering an alert that brought multiple armed patrol cars despite officials quickly confirming there was no threat. The lawsuit says the school's AI system has a false-positive rate above 99%, and the students say the police response traumatized them.
items.https://techcrunch.com/2026/11/19/anthro: Anthropic went public, raising $81.3 billion total including $1.95 billion from its seven founders, who each sold about 3.4 million shares at the upgraded $83 IPO price for roughly $280 million apiece before fees and taxes - more than the $250 million they had targeted. Anthropic says each founder has pledged 80% of their personal equity to philanthropy, though they can scale back that commitment if needed.
items.https://inc42.com/buzz/indias-anthropic-: Anthropic's blockbuster IPO has sparked debate over whether India can build a globally competitive AI company of its own, after Kotak Mahindra founder Uday Kotak noted Anthropic's $1.5 trillion valuation exceeds India's ten biggest firms combined. While domestic AI startups raised a record $1.1 billion in the first nine months of 2026, most funding went to applied "vertical AI" rather than foundational research, leaving a talent and research gap.
items.https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/tec: Meta plans to price its Muse Charm AI wearable at $300, The Information reported. Unveiled in September by CEO Mark Zuckerberg, the device carries Meta's Muse AI agent into the real world, part of Meta's push to lessen reliance on Apple and Google's operating systems.
items.https://inc42.com/buzz/ai-startup-disseq: Irish AI governance startup Disseqt AI, whose engineering team is based in Bengaluru, raised $8 million (about ₹75 crore) in a round led by Gresham House Ventures, with Sure Valley Ventures, Delta Partners, Enterprise Ireland and cricketer Rahul Dravid also participating. The company builds AI agents that test and govern other AI agents, and will use the funds to expand enterprise customers across the UK and international markets.
